_doc: Test pack 'test_hamlet' (Phase 013b): MAJOR_ACTIONS. Authored, copied, or empty as recorded in docs/phases/phase013b/PHASE013B_REPORT.md. Copied values keep their citations in packs/bigville.

move.description: Walk to a destination the affordances offer. Travel takes time and energy, more on rough ground.

give.description: Hand a held good to a person in reach who has room to carry it. The world moves the goods. It does not decide whether the handover is a sale.

attempt.description: Try any physical action on a thing within reach, by a verb the world has physics for (smash, chop, pry, force, push, pull, drag). A thing on the ground is moved by push, pull or drag; a container is damaged or forced. Name the verb, the target, the tool you hold (if any), and an intensity (1.0 is normal; more forces it, less is gentler). The world resolves it from your strength, skill, the tool, the target and your stamina, and reports the progress, damage and noise it sees. A verb the world has no physics for is refused as unsupported.

take.description: Take held goods, coin, or an item from a person standing on your cell. The holder may resist, brace, yield, or step away. The outcome depends on strength, size, skill, and stamina; the world does not decide whether the taking is theft.

strike.description: Strike a person standing on your cell with your bare hands. Name the target and an intensity (1.0 is a normal blow; less is a pull, more forces it), and optionally a region of the target's body to aim at, given as params region (head, chest, back, arm or leg). An aimed blow lands on that region with some chance; otherwise it lands where the blow falls. The blow's harm and its cost come from your strength, size, skill and stamina, against what the target does: it may resist, brace, step away, or take the blow. A blow with little stamina left lands weakly. The world records the blow as a physical event for those who can see you; it does not judge whether the blow was justified.

restrain.description: Take hold of a person standing on your cell, to keep them where they are. They may resist, brace, yield, or step away; the outcome depends on strength, size, skill and stamina. While you hold them they cannot walk, and you cannot walk either until you let go. Holding costs stamina each turn for both of you. The world records the grab for those who can see it; it does not judge whether the holding is justified.

release.description: Let go of the person you are holding. Their hold ends, and both of you may walk again.

struggle.description: While someone holds you, try to pull free. The outcome depends on your strength, size, skill and stamina against theirs. Winning frees you; losing leaves you held. Both of you spend stamina on the struggle.

put.description: Place a held good into a container or onto a surface within reach.

pick_up.description: Take up an item lying within reach, if there is room to carry it.

drop.description: Set a held item down where you stand.

sell.description: Retired: the world refuses this action (it returns false). To hand over goods, use give.

sell_labor.description: Retired: the world refuses this action (it returns false). Work is done with work.

work.description: Carry out one recipe at a workplace in reach, using the inputs, tools, and skill the affordance names.

eat.description: Eat food you hold or that is at hand, to reduce hunger.

water.description: Water a field or plot in reach.

sleep.description: Lie down and sleep. Sleep restores energy at a steady rate until you are rested, and you cannot act until you wake. You fall asleep where you stand if your energy runs out.

fetch.description: Fetch an amount of one kind of goods from a source the affordance names, and bring it to you.

build.description: Build or continue a building project at a site in reach.

harvest.description: Harvest a ready crop from a field in reach.

sow.description: Sow seed in a prepared field in reach.

fertilise.description: Spread fertiliser on a field in reach.

tend_animals.description: Tend an animal or a pen in reach, for the task the affordance names.

maintain.description: Maintain a building, tool, or fixture in reach.

care.description: Care for a person or an animal in reach who needs it.

lock.description: Lock a container you hold the key to, or the town store, from the cell it stands on. The key must be in your hand or carried by you.

unlock.description: Unlock a locked container or the town store with a key you hold, from the cell it stands on. A lock that needs several keyholders opens only after that many of them have unlocked it.
